name: Ubir
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm D. 1988. Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian languages of western Melanesia (Pacific Linguistics C-98). Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online: WID Offsite Storage PL6201.R67 1988 (also: archive.org controlled lending)
sources.note: Ubir cited only as reflexes in Proto Papuan Tip reconstructions (37 mentions, ch. 6); stress remarks in the book concern Schouten/Ali etc., none for Ubir.

sources.citation: Ray, Sidney H. 1907. The Melanesian languages of British New Guinea. In Reports of the Cambridge Anthropological Expedition to Torres Straits, vol. III (Linguistics), 413-503. Cambridge: CUP.
sources.note: Kubiri (=Ubir), Raqa, Kiviri, Oiun: pronoun paradigms (§30) and comparative sound correspondences; no accent or stress remark for Kubiri anywhere in the section.

sources.citation: SIL Language & Culture Archives listing for ubr, Wayback capture 2015-09-17 (http://web.archive.org/web/20150917233945/http://www.sil.org/resources/search/language/ubr).
sources.note: In 2015 SIL listed only two Bible Translator articles (divine-names case studies) for ubr; no phonology (OPD) or grammar file existed in the archive then.

sources.citation: Capell, Arthur. 1976. Austronesian and Papuan "mixed" languages: general remarks. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study, vol. 2 (Pacific Linguistics C-39), 527-579. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Ubir forms appear in comparative tables (Wedau/Mukawa/Ubir/Maisin, pp. ~540-575); the only 'stress' passages concern Germanic. Silent on Ubir stress.

sources.citation: Lithgow, David R. 1976. Austronesian languages: Milne Bay and adjacent islands (Milne Bay Province). In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study, vol. 2: Austronesian languages (Pacific Linguistics C-39), 441-523. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: §84 STRESS (p. 475) is a regional statement about the Milne Bay 'PTC' languages ('Stress is phonemic in Kilivila, Muyuw, Budibud, Misima...'; 'In all of the languages of PTC it seems that stress is predictable within certain word-classes, notably kinship nouns and verbs'); Ubir is treated separately as a Northern Province language in §73 (p. 471: subject prefixes, two possession classes, 'Words tend to be shorter in these languages, and there are many word-final consonants') and is not named in the stress section. Silent on Ubir stress.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Ubir language' (stub; links to a 1920 Anglican prayer book in Ubir and to PARADISEC).
Grambank language page for Ubir (ubir1237), coder Julia Rizaew; Grambank sources.bib entry s_Boreret_Ubir.
sources.note: Confirms Boreret et al. 2015 is the sole source used for Ubir; gives no URL and no phonological information.

sources.citation: Boreret, Bray, Bradley Aira & Jason Carwile. 2015. Tentative Grammar Description for the Ubir [ubi] Language spoken in Oro Province. Ms., 48 pp. SIL PNG (Grammar Essentials workshop series).

sources.access_detail: open link recorded by Glottolog or the catalog, not checked; access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: The only descriptive source for Ubir on record (Glottolog hhtype grammar_sketch; the sole Grambank source). SIL PNG tentative grammar descriptions normally open with a phonology/orthography summary where a stress statement would sit. Should be requested from SIL PNG (pnglanguages.sil.org archive) or from Harald Hammarström (hh file papua/).

sources.citation: Strong, W. M. 1911. Notes on the languages of the north-eastern and adjoining divisions. Papua Annual Report for the year ending 30th June 1911, 203-217.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Earliest grammatical notes on the Collingwood Bay languages including Ubir/Kubiri (Glottolog 309606, hhtype wordlist); low chance of an accent remark, but the only pre-2015 primary material beyond wordlists. Papua Annual Reports are not on archive.org (search returned 0); print/ANU-library only.
